title: This Lizard Runs Across Water. The Trick Is What's Under Its Feet
subject: basilisk lizard

scenes.text: This lizard can run across a lake. The trick is a pocket of air.
The basilisk slaps each foot straight down onto the water, pushing the water away and trapping air around the foot.
The lizard pushes off against the wall of that air cavity, then pulls the foot out before the water closes in.
It can keep this up for about fifteen feet, at around five feet per second.
It only works while moving. Stop, and it sinks and swims.
Babies do it best. A hatchling weighs about two grams, an adult up to two hundred. So yes: it runs on air.
